logline: The Shelby family controls Birmingham's criminal underworld in interwar England - Tommy Shelby building an empire through violence, politics, and the kind of cold intelligence that looks, from a distance, like genius.

renewal.note: Concluded after 6 series on April 3, 2022; a feature film adaptation was in development as of mid-2026.

bollymeter.basis: Strong critical reception on BBC Two. The show introduced Cillian Murphy as Tommy Shelby - a performance built on stillness and calculation that became the defining British TV lead of the decade. The anachronistic soundtrack (Nick Cave, PJ Harvey) signalled that this was not heritage drama.

pull_quotes.text: Cillian Murphy's Tommy Shelby is a commanding creation - Peaky Blinders announces itself as British TV's most stylistically assured new drama.

seasons.review_body: The debut series of Peaky Blinders arrived on BBC Two to solid reviews and modest ratings - its global reputation was built retrospectively through Netflix distribution. Steven Knight's creation of Birmingham's Shelby family is distinguished by the combination of rigorous period authenticity and deliberate anachronism: the soundtrack, the styling, the refusal to treat the 1919 setting as heritage. Cillian Murphy's Tommy Shelby is the key: a First World War veteran running a criminal gang with the tactical intelligence of a military commander and the emotional vacancy of someone hollowed out by what he survived. Sam Neill's Inspector Campbell is the adversary the pilot needed to establish stakes. The six-episode run is tight and economical; the world is fully built.

bollymeter.basis: The show's expansion into London's criminal underworld and the introduction of Tom Hardy's Alfie Solomons - the scene-stealing performance that became the series' most beloved secondary character. The show's confidence grew visibly.

pull_quotes.text: Peaky Blinders reaches new heights in its second series - Tom Hardy's Alfie Solomons is a scene-stealing force of nature.

seasons.review_body: Series 2 is where the show found its global audience and its most flamboyant asset. Tom Hardy's Alfie Solomons - Jewish gangster, Rum Runner, philosophical chaos agent - arrived and immediately became the show's most discussed character. Hardy plays the role as a controlled explosion: every scene with Murphy's Tommy is a negotiation between two performers who are both operating at maximum intensity. The London expansion and the Italian-Jewish gang war give the show a historical scale that the first series' Birmingham setting couldn't support. The cinematography deepens: Steven Knight and director Colm McCarthy develop the show's distinctive aesthetic of fog, coal-light, and deliberate anachronism. By S2's end, Peaky Blinders had become appointment viewing.
seasons.season_over_season: The show's international breakthrough: expanded geography, Tom Hardy, and a more confident claim on its own aesthetic.

bollymeter.basis: The Russian aristocracy and Soviet espionage arc; Tommy in Parliament; the show at its most geopolitically ambitious. Paddy Considine's Father Hughes is the most frightening antagonist in the run. Critical consensus solidifies the show as prestige television.

pull_quotes.text: Series 3 is Peaky Blinders at its most ambitious - Tommy Shelby on the international stage, with Cillian Murphy delivering his finest performance in the role.

seasons.review_body: Series 3 is where Peaky Blinders made its play for international prestige status. The Russian emigre aristocracy, the Soviet OGPU, and Tommy's entanglement with both through a gun-running operation give the show its most globally sophisticated canvas. Paddy Considine's Father Hughes - a paedophile priest protected by his usefulness to the state - is used sparingly and is the more terrifying for it. The finale's mass Shelby family arrest is the show's most operatic season close. Tommy's entrance into Parliament is handled with the same visual ambition as the show's best fight sequences. Critics recognised that Steven Knight was managing a complex network of period detail and pulp pleasure with increasing confidence.
seasons.season_over_season: International in scale and darker in register - the show's most politically complex season and arguably its creative peak.

bollymeter.basis: Adrien Brody as Luca Changretta; the Italian-American mafia war; the show's tightest seasonal plot. Tom Hardy returns. The season most often cited as the best by fans who prioritise forward momentum and villain quality.

pull_quotes.text: Series 4 is Peaky Blinders' most propulsive season - Adrien Brody's Changretta is a worthy adversary and Tom Hardy's return is electric.

seasons.review_body: The most propulsive Peaky Blinders season, structured as a tightly wound war between the Shelbys and the Changretta family. Adrien Brody's Luca Changretta arrives from New York with a vendetta and the patience to execute it; he is the show's most conventionally dangerous antagonist and the series is better for having someone who simply wants the Shelbys dead rather than wanting to use them. Tom Hardy's Alfie Solomons returns with maximum disruption. The boxing match climax is the show's single best constructed action set-piece. The Polly-Tommy dynamic deepens: Helen McCrory's performance is the season's quiet best. Fans who rank this as the series' peak cite its clean narrative architecture; critics and IMDb audiences gave it the show's highest audience rating to this point.
seasons.season_over_season: The tightest plot in the franchise's run - a focused vengeance thriller with the show's best antagonist.

bollymeter.basis: The Wall Street crash, the rise of British fascism, Oswald Mosley. Sam Claflin as Mosley is the season's most culturally resonant casting. The season's conclusion - a conspiracy that fails ambiguously - divides viewers but is arguably the show's most politically serious writing.

pull_quotes.text: Series 5 broadens Peaky Blinders' political canvas dramatically - Sam Claflin's Mosley is alarming, and the show's fascism parallels land with uncomfortable relevance.

seasons.review_body: Series 5 is Peaky Blinders at its most historically serious. The 1929 stock market crash and the rise of British Union of Fascists gives Steven Knight his most pointed contemporary allegory - Sam Claflin's Oswald Mosley is an explicitly political creation that generated real comment on broadcast. The season's narrative ambition outpaces its six-episode runtime: the anti-Mosley conspiracy feels compressed, and the finale's conclusion - which is deliberately ambiguous about whether the plan succeeded - frustrated viewers who wanted resolution. Tommy's mental deterioration thread is the season's best characterisation. Helen McCrory as Polly is again the ensemble's moral anchor. The show has reached the point where its reach occasionally exceeds its grasp.
seasons.season_over_season: More politically ambitious but more structurally strained - the six-episode format is too small for the history the season tries to hold.

bollymeter.basis: The final series, made under the shadow of Helen McCrory's death in 2021. Polly Gray's absence restructures the show in ways the writing honestly acknowledges rather than writes around. The finale closes Tommy's arc with ambiguity; critics divided on whether it constitutes an ending.

pull_quotes.text: A final series shaped by real-world grief - Peaky Blinders ends with dignity, though not the definitive conclusion the show deserved.

seasons.review_body: Series 6 is a final season that is impossible to evaluate separately from its circumstances. Helen McCrory died in April 2021 before filming; the series addresses Polly Gray's absence directly, in a tribute that the show handles with genuine emotional weight. Cillian Murphy's Tommy navigates a storyline involving opium addiction, a fatal diagnosis, and a final confrontation with fascism that carries the weight of everything the show has spent six series building. The finale - open enough that a film continuation was immediately planned - is contested: some read it as a bold refusal to provide conventional closure, others as an incomplete conclusion. Critics gave the series a respectful reception; audiences were slightly more divided. Murphy's performance is the best argument for the series' conclusion.
seasons.season_over_season: Made under profound real-world constraints and honoring those constraints honestly - the ending is incomplete by design and circumstance.
